title: THE LIBRARY AT THE EDGE OF NOISE
deck: A library hidden in the hiss between galaxies answers any question perfectly and takes one memory from whoever asks. With famine closing on three worlds, Illuminara must discover what the Library is really charging for, teach it where an answer may safely land, and wait long enough to prove that the answer works.
shape: Five scenes: an inventory of what the Library has taken and the discovery that it consumes highly recoverable structure, not preciousness; a personless test using a true parity-linked calibration grid; a failed clone lattice followed by a varied, self-repairing host that is shown to take only a declared host before the captain trusts it; a famine rule whose two blanks Illuminara fills from a single anomalous convoy and that Ossel's delegate contests and bargains down; and a sixty-one-day checkpoint with a controlled host-choice trial, while the earliest losses remain lost.

scenes.title: The Price of an Answer
paragraphs: *Survey vessel Tamsin Reach, three million light-years beyond the Calder Rim · ship-day 211, 06:10*

The Library had never spoken first. It lay in the hiss between galaxies, in what every instrument on the Tamsin Reach insisted was noise, and the crew could read it only by asking. Ask a question and the noise folded itself into a complete answer, exact to the last digit. A moment later the person who had asked reached for something and found it gone.

Captain Hadiza Moreau had lost the name of her first ship. Navigator Soren Eklund could still see the photographs of his wife, but they no longer meant her. Bartosz Wende, the linguist, had asked for bread at supper and found that Lowvale, the language his grandmother had spoken to him, had left him between one sentence and the next.

Illuminara stood at the question console with her hands behind her back. Nobody had told her not to touch it. She had simply understood, on arriving, that the console was the only dangerous object aboard.

**Hadiza**  
Eleven questions, five of us paid. We asked it about the Calder famine in pieces because the whole is too large to ask. The pieces are right. They do not add up. The relief fleet is six hundred ships, and every correction we send makes the next shortage worse. Tarn runs dry in forty days, Veyra in sixty, and Ossel after that. Forty million people. The model needs one answer we cannot compute, and the only place that answer lives is behind that console.

**Bartosz**  
And the price is us. Tell her, Hadiza. Tell her what it takes.

**Illuminara**  
I would rather you told me what it took. Exactly. Not what it cost you.

They gave her the list slowly, in the flat voices of people reading an inventory after a fire. A ship's name. A face. A language. Two lullabies. The way to tie a bowline, which the ship's cook had had for sixty years and now could not do with her own hands.

Illuminara asked for the neural rehearsal maps recorded before and after each loss. Moreau hesitated, then released only the anonymous structural traces. No images, names or private associations left the medical vault.

*Not the rare things,* Illuminara thought. *Not the secrets. The patterns with the most alternate paths back to themselves.* Moreau had written that ship's name on forms for forty years. Soren had looked at that face every morning. Bartosz had said Lowvale to himself each night for three decades, with nobody left to hear it.

**Illuminara**  
Everything it has taken is something your mind could reconstruct from many overlapping routes. The pattern was precious to you. To the transmission, it was highly recoverable structure.

**Bartosz**  
It was the part of me that was me.

**Illuminara**  
To you, yes. I think to it, it looked like room where errors could be checked without destroying the message. I do not yet know whether it can tell room from a person. That is the question I want to test before anyone asks it anything else.

scenes.title: A Question With No One Behind It
paragraphs: *Instrument bay · 09:40*

She did not ask the console. She went aft to the survey array, a rack of sensors that could send a query without any person standing behind it, and asked Soren what part of the array could survive being partly erased.

**Soren**  
The calibration matrix. Four thousand and ninety-six different rows. Every reading is crossed by twelve parity relations, so any missing quarter can be rebuilt from the rest. The raw sky data has a separate vault copy. Why?

**Illuminara**  
Because I have two predictions and they disagree. If the Library charges people, the array will pay nothing. If it borrows the receiver's most recoverable structure as an error-checking host, the matrix will go. Not because its rows repeat, but because each row can be recovered through many different rows.
She wrote both predictions on a card, folded it and gave it to Bartosz, who held it like a man given a stranger's coat. Then she asked Soren to erase one row in eight.
The array rebuilt every erased row. A green figure appeared beneath the matrix: reconstruction confidence, nine nines after the decimal. Illuminara pointed to it.

**Illuminara**  
That is the signature. A valid host is not a pile of copies. It is a structure that still knows what was removed.
She had the array ask the plainest question the crew could verify: how many days had passed since the Reach's keel was laid.

The noise folded. The array received four thousand and eighteen, which the ship's records confirmed to the day. At the same instant, the parity links in the calibration matrix turned to white static. The raw measurements remained. The relations that could have rebuilt them were gone.
Soren deleted another row. This time the array could not restore it.

**Bartosz**  
It took from a machine.

**Illuminara**  
It took the machine's most recoverable structure. The answer arrived wrapped in more correction than empty space could hold. It used the receiver's own cross-checks as the missing part of its channel.

**Hadiza**  
And a mind offers better cross-checks than any instrument.

**Illuminara**  
Because we rehearse what we love. Each rehearsal becomes another path home. The more routes a memory has, the more useful it is to a message trying to survive this distance.

**Bartosz**  
Then it is a thief that does not know it steals.

**Illuminara**  
Or a postman who pads every parcel with whatever furniture can be rebuilt. I would not forgive him on that account. But I would know what kind of furniture to put by the door.

Soren restored the calibration matrix from the vault in six minutes. Nobody in the bay said that nothing could restore a language from a vault. Bartosz folded the card smaller and smaller until it would fold no more.

scenes.title: Furniture
paragraphs: *Cargo hold three · 14:30*

The first lattice was Illuminara's design, and it was the crew who built it. Coolant crystal rose from the deck in a clear scaffold. Into it they recorded the day's log, the engine counts and the galley songs until the hold contained nine hundred copies of each.
She insisted on three rules, and said them aloud so they could be argued with.

**Illuminara**  
Nobody puts in anything they would grieve. Copies only, never originals, and nothing that is the only copy of anything. The lattice is cheap on purpose. Anyone may refuse. Whoever refuses is not asked again.

**Soren**  
My wife's photographs are not going in that crystal.

**Illuminara**  
They are not. Neither are you.
He looked at her for a long time. Then he went to the galley and began singing the supper song into the recorder, off-key, nine hundred times.

She asked Bartosz for the card. Beneath her two predictions she wrote a third, in the same hand: *Nine hundred copies will serve as a host.* She gave it back to him folded, and then she asked him to erase one song from the lattice.

Eight hundred and ninety-nine identical copies remained, but none held a relation that could say what had been erased rather than merely replace it with another clone. The reconstruction display stayed red.

**Bartosz**  
A pile of the same chair. No room between them.

**Illuminara**  
The display disagrees with my third line. A prediction that disagrees with its instrument is worth sending anyway, so we will find out which of them is wrong.

They sent the clone lattice with a trivial question. The noise did not fold. For four hours the hiss between galaxies stayed hiss, and in those four hours Moreau said, in a voice she kept very level, that perhaps the Library had refused them.
Illuminara did not rename the silence a success. She asked Bartosz to open the card, and she wrote FAILED beneath the third line herself.

**Illuminara**  
The array survived erasure because its differences checked one another. A wall of the same chair cannot do that. The display was right and I was wrong.

Then she built variation into the host. Each song was sung in a different key, at a different speed and by a different mixture of voices. Engine counts were grouped across independent clocks. Logs were split into fragments whose parity lines crossed the songs without containing them. Wren Odira, who had come aboard with the courier and sang flat, supplied forty recordings nobody else could reproduce.
They erased one fragment in eight. The lattice restored every one from relationships that crossed unlike material. The display turned green: the same nine nines as the survey matrix.

**Wren**  
Ugly enough?

**Illuminara**  
Rich enough. It can lose part of itself and still know what belonged there.
They placed a declaration at the front of the code: HOST LATTICE THREE. Nothing in the declaration named a person. Nothing pointed at the ship's medical network.

Before anything else was sent, she asked every soul aboard to seal one thing on a slip of paper that they could still name today and would grieve to lose. Moreau wrote her daughter's name. Soren wrote the street where he had proposed. Bartosz, who had nothing of Lowvale left to guard, wrote the date his grandmother died, the one fact about her that still held.
Soren set the array to send the question. Nobody stood at the console, and nobody touched it. It asked for the number of engine cycles since the last refit.

The noise folded. The answer arrived, and the ship's logs confirmed it to the cycle. In the hold the lattice's parity relations went to static while the recordings stayed whole in the vault. Then they opened the slips, one by one, and read each against the mind that had written it. Every slip held.

**Hadiza**  
It took the host. Only the host.

**Illuminara**  
Once. In front of us, with no one at the console. That is one trial, and one trial is not a rule. But it is the first thing we have seen that tells us the declaration changes where it writes.

Moreau asked the first real question herself. Nothing required it now. She did it because she would not send anyone to stand where she would not, and because a captain who trusts a result ought to be able to put her hand on it. She asked standing, with her palm flat on the console, and reached for her own name, and her own name was there.
The crystal rang faintly, like a glass someone had touched.

scenes.title: The Rule
paragraphs: *Ship's long room · ship-day 212, 02:15*

The answer was not a number. It was a shape, and it took them four hours to read it. Hold back a fixed share of each world's reserve before shipping anything. Release not in proportion to the shortage but in proportion to the lag between order and arrival. The cascade, Illuminara said, was a ringing: every ship corrected for a hunger already a week old, and the corrections starved the next world down the line.
It was exact, and it had two blanks. The share and the lag. The Library had never seen the fleet's ledgers, so it could not have filled them.

She asked for the logs of every ship and the ledgers of all three worlds, set them side by side, and read for what did not fit. It was the third hour before it did. A grain convoy out of Tarn, eighteen ships, had reached Veyra's gate nine days after dispatch. Tarn's ledger carried it as in transit for fourteen. Veyra's ledger did not count it until customs stamped the manifest on the fourteenth day.

**Illuminara**  
For five days that grain stood in a warehouse at Veyra's gate and was in nobody's ledger. Tarn had written it off. Veyra had not yet written it on. Every world down the line is reading stamps, not grain.

**Soren**  
One convoy. A freak.

**Illuminara**  
I checked the forty nearest. The same gap appears in every one, between three and four percent of outgoing stock in any three-day window. A shortage that is only paperwork.

**Hadiza**  
Then part of the famine is a stamp.

**Illuminara**  
Part of the ringing is. That fills the blanks. The true lag is nine days, not fourteen. And anything under four percent is what the stamps explain. Outgoing stock exceeding incoming by more than four percent in two three-day windows running is real hunger. The hold changes at once. No world waits for a beautiful model to admit it is wrong.
Nobody on the Reach cheered. They were looking at the line that said Ossel must hold its stores for eleven days while its own people went short.
Delegate Aurelio Quist of Ossel appeared on the delay link in the grey light of his morning, forty minutes behind the words he was answering.

**Aurelio Quist**  
You are asking my people to sit on full warehouses for eleven days on the word of a voice in the static. My southern districts are hungry now. I will not sign that.

**Illuminara**  
I cannot sign for you and I will not try. May I show you the whole damped model, with its margin of error, the convoy that gave us the lag, and the places where it hurts Ossel first?
She showed him. She showed him the Marrow convoy's two ledgers side by side, and she showed him the southern districts in red. She did not hide them behind an average.

**Aurelio Quist**  
Eight days, not eleven. Hospitals and school kitchens come out of the hold by right. And my analysts receive the raw ledger, not your conclusions.

**Illuminara**  
Your own list puts hospitals and school kitchens at eleven percent of Ossel's draw. Add three points so the exception can rotate by public lot and no district can buy it, and eight days works. Fourteen percent. Your analysts should hold the stop condition with ours. I can ask the Library to check the arithmetic. The host will pay, not a mind.

**Hadiza**  
Another lattice.

**Wren**  
I have six hundred more songs. All of them flat.

The second answer came back at dawn and confirmed the arithmetic: eight days, with a fourteen percent rotating exception, held the forecast inside bounds that Quist's analysts could reproduce from the raw ledger. It did not promise to make anyone whole. His southern districts would be short for three weeks, and some of the old and very young might not survive. Quist signed with that warning beside his name, because he would not sign without it.

scenes.title: What Was Not Returned
paragraphs: *Observation deck · ship-day 274, 21:00*
Sixty-one days had passed since the first rule entered the fleet. That morning, analysts from Tarn, Veyra and Ossel had signed separate ledgers without sharing their conclusions first.

Tarn's stores had never reached empty and now held nineteen days of food. Veyra had bottomed at twelve percent reserve before rising for twenty-one consecutive days. Ossel's southern districts had endured the promised shortage; one hundred and eighty-three people had died whose deaths the delegates judged famine-related. Forty million was the figure the old orders had produced when the fleet's logs were run forward without the rule. It was a forecast, and every ledger said so. The ledgers recorded only what had happened.

The four-percent trigger had fired once, on Veyra. Ossel's analysts had demanded the agreed correction, three convoys had turned and the next two windows returned below threshold. The rule had not been trusted. It had been watched.

Before the relief fleet dispersed, the crew had run one more test the famine did not require, the controlled version of what they had seen once. They built two harmless self-repairing hosts, amber and blue, each carrying the same trivial question and a different random nonce. The declaration named amber.
The Library answered once. Amber's parity relations vanished. Blue remained whole.
They cleared the local receiver, rebuilt both hosts from untouched backups, reversed their positions and named blue. The Library answered again. Blue paid. Amber did not.

Then the Library did something it had never done. For one hundred and four seconds the hiss at the console took on a plain repeating shape: the host field, empty, followed by the nonce it had been offered. It did not say yes. It asked where.

**Hadiza**  
Twice is not a conscience.

**Illuminara**  
No. It is a choice we can tell apart from outage, local formatting or chance. We know it can follow a declared host. We do not know what following means to it.

**Bartosz**  
So it was a language we had not learned.

**Illuminara**  
A first word of one. It can still refuse a host. It can still remain silent. We have only stopped making a person the default address.
Bartosz stood at the glass with his back to them. After a while he spoke, in a voice that had gone careful, as one speaks a second language.

**Bartosz**  
Can the lattice give it back? The Lowvale. I would put myself into the crystal if it would.
Illuminara would have given a great deal to answer otherwise.

**Illuminara**  
No. The Library took the only copy that ever lived in you, and nothing in the lattice is a copy of it. I can build you a better scaffold. I cannot build you a grandmother. If I said I could, I would be doing to you what the Library did, in a gentler voice.
He nodded, and he did not turn around. Then he asked Wren, who sang flat, to teach him one of her songs. He said he had a good deal of room.

The Calder worlds allowed one question a fortnight, no more. Every question required a named external host, two successful reconstruction tests, public consent for the material used and an independent watcher holding the stop key. No person was asked to forget how to make the channel safe.
Illuminara did not ask the Library anything herself. She stayed a while at the console, and the hiss lay quiet beneath her palm.
*A perfect answer,* she thought, *had only ever been badly addressed.*

critic_line: A silent library that charges a memory per answer is answered not with force but with a test it could be wrong about, and Illuminara's patience, her own failed prediction and a paperwork anomaly in a freight ledger feed three worlds without another person paying for it.

literary_score.method: Equal-weight mean of locked independent blind final evaluations of the exact English final
shared_strengths: Both evaluations recognized the explicit failed prediction, the varied host test and the ledger anomaly as an earned path from hypothesis to rescue.
The famine response is observed after the relevant delay, preserves Quist’s negotiating authority and leaves the earliest memory losses unrepaired.
shared_reservations: Both evaluations found the parity and host explanations dense, with briefing-like dialogue sometimes displacing dramatic friction.
The clone-lattice failure and final aphorism make the mechanism feel neater and more certain than the story’s own careful qualifications.

translation_sl.title: KNJIŽNICA NA ROBU ŠUMA
translation_sl.deck: Knjižnica, skrita v šumenju med galaksijami, brezhibno odgovori na vsako vprašanje in vsakemu, ki vpraša, vzame en spomin. Ko lakota stiska tri svetove, mora Illuminara odkriti, kaj Knjižnica v resnici zaračunava, jo naučiti, kam lahko odgovor varno prispe, in čakati dovolj dolgo, da dokaže, da odgovor deluje.
translation_sl.shape: Pet prizorov: popis tega, kar je Knjižnica vzela, in odkritje, da porablja zelo obnovljivo strukturo, ne dragocenosti; preizkus brez človeka z resnično kalibracijsko mrežo, povezano s paritetami; spodletela mreža klonov, ki ji sledi raznolik, samoobnovljiv gostitelj, za katerega se pokaže, da vzame samo razglašenega gostitelja, preden mu kapitanka zaupa; pravilo za lakoto, katerega dve praznini Illuminara zapolni iz enega nenavadnega konvoja in ki mu Osselov delegat ugovarja ter ga izpogaja navzdol; in kontrolna točka po enainšestdesetih dneh z nadzorovanim preizkusom izbire gostitelja, medtem ko najzgodnejše izgube ostanejo izgubljene.

scenes.title: Cena odgovora
paragraphs: *Raziskovalna ladja Tamsin Reach, tri milijone svetlobnih let onkraj Calderjevega roba · 211. ladijski dan, 06:10*

Knjižnica ni nikoli spregovorila prva. Ležala je v šumenju med galaksijami, v tistem, kar so vsi instrumenti na ladji Tamsin Reach razglašali za šum, posadka pa jo je lahko brala le tako, da je spraševala. Zastavi vprašanje in šum se je zložil v popoln odgovor, natančen do zadnje števke. Trenutek zatem je človek, ki je vprašal, segel po nečem in ugotovil, da tega ni več.

Kapitanka Hadiza Moreau je izgubila ime svoje prve ladje. Navigator Soren Eklund je še vedno videl fotografije svoje žene, vendar mu niso več pomenile nje. Jezikoslovec Bartosz Wende je pri večerji prosil za kruh in ugotovil, da ga je Lowvale, jezik, v katerem mu je govorila babica, zapustil med enim in drugim stavkom.
Illuminara je stala pri vprašalnem pultu z rokami za hrbtom. Nihče ji ni rekel, naj se ga ne dotika. Ob prihodu je preprosto razumela, da je pult edini nevarni predmet na krovu.

**Hadiza**  
Enajst vprašanj, pet od nas je plačalo. O lakoti v Calderju smo jo spraševali po delih, ker je celota prevelika za eno vprašanje. Deli so pravilni. Ne sestavijo se. Pomožna flota šteje šeststo ladij in vsak popravek, ki ga pošljemo, naslednje pomanjkanje še poslabša. Tarn bo brez zalog v štiridesetih dneh, Veyra v šestdesetih, Ossel pa zatem. Štirideset milijonov ljudi. Model potrebuje en odgovor, ki ga ne moremo izračunati, in edini kraj, kjer ta odgovor obstaja, je za tem pultom.

**Bartosz**  
In cena smo mi. Povej ji, Hadiza. Povej ji, kaj vzame.

**Illuminara**  
Raje bi, da mi vi poveste, kaj je vzelo. Natančno. Ne, kaj vas je stalo.

Seznam so ji podajali počasi, z ravnimi glasovi ljudi, ki po požaru berejo popis. Ime ladje. Obraz. Jezik. Dve uspavanki. Način vezanja pašnjega vozla, ki ga je ladijska kuharica poznala šestdeset let, zdaj pa ga z lastnimi rokami ni več znala zavezati.

Illuminara je prosila za zemljevide nevronskih ponovitev, posnete pred vsako izgubo in po njej. Moreau je oklevala, nato pa izdala le anonimne strukturne sledi. Nobena slika, ime ali zasebna povezava ni zapustila zdravstvenega trezorja.

*Ne redkih stvari,* je pomislila Illuminara. *Ne skrivnosti. Vzorcev z največ nadomestnimi potmi nazaj do samih sebe.* Moreau je ime tiste ladje štirideset let zapisovala na obrazce. Soren je tisti obraz gledal vsako jutro. Bartosz si je Lowvale tri desetletja vsak večer govoril sam pri sebi, ko ni bilo nikogar več, ki bi ga slišal.

**Illuminara**  
Vse, kar je vzelo, je nekaj, kar je vaš um lahko rekonstruiral po številnih prekrivajočih se poteh. Vzorec je bil za vas dragocen. Za prenos je bil zelo obnovljiva struktura.

**Bartosz**  
To je bil del mene, zaradi katerega sem bil jaz.

**Illuminara**  
Za vas da. Mislim, da je prenos v njem videl prostor, kjer je mogoče preveriti napake, ne da bi uničil sporočilo. Še ne vem, ali zna razlikovati prostor od človeka. To želim preizkusiti, preden ga kdo vpraša karkoli drugega.

scenes.title: Vprašanje brez človeka za njim
paragraphs: *Oddelek z instrumenti · 09:40*

Ni vprašala pulta. Odšla je na krmo k raziskovalnemu sklopu, stojalu senzorjev, ki je lahko poslalo vprašanje, ne da bi za njim stal človek, in Sorena vprašala, kateri del sklopa bi preživel delni izbris.

**Soren**  
Kalibracijska matrika. Štiri tisoč šestindevetdeset različnih vrstic. Vsak odčitek križa dvanajst paritetnih razmerij, zato lahko iz preostanka obnovimo katerokoli manjkajočo četrtino. Surovi podatki neba imajo ločeno kopijo v trezorju. Zakaj?

**Illuminara**  
Ker imam dve napovedi in si nasprotujeta. Če Knjižnica zaračunava ljudem, sklop ne bo plačal ničesar. Če si kot gostitelja za odpravljanje napak izposodi najbolj obnovljivo strukturo sprejemnika, bo izginila matrika. Ne zato, ker se njene vrstice ponavljajo, temveč zato, ker je vsako vrstico mogoče obnoviti prek številnih drugih vrstic.
Obe napovedi je zapisala na kartico, jo prepognila in dala Bartoszu, ki jo je držal kakor človek, ki so mu izročili tuj plašč. Nato je Sorena prosila, naj izbriše vsako osmo vrstico.
Sklop je obnovil vsako izbrisano vrstico. Pod matriko se je prikazala zelena številka: zanesljivost rekonstrukcije z devetimi devetkami za decimalno vejico. Illuminara je pokazala nanjo.

**Illuminara**  
To je podpis. Veljaven gostitelj ni kup kopij. Je struktura, ki še vedno ve, kaj je bilo odstranjeno.
Sklopu je naročila, naj zastavi najbolj preprosto vprašanje, ki ga je posadka lahko preverila: koliko dni je minilo, odkar so položili kobilico ladje Reach.

Šum se je zložil. Sklop je prejel štiri tisoč osemnajst, kar so ladijski zapisi potrdili do dneva natančno. V istem trenutku so se paritetne povezave v kalibracijski matriki spremenile v beli šum. Surove meritve so ostale. Razmerij, ki bi jih lahko obnovila, ni bilo več.
Soren je izbrisal še eno vrstico. Tokrat je sklop ni mogel obnoviti.

**Bartosz**  
Vzela je stroju.

**Illuminara**  
Vzela je najbolj obnovljivo strukturo stroja. Odgovor je prispel ovit v več popravkov, kot jih je lahko nosil prazen prostor. Kot manjkajoči del svojega kanala je uporabil sprejemnikova lastna navzkrižna preverjanja.

**Hadiza**  
In um ponuja boljša navzkrižna preverjanja kot katerikoli instrument.

**Illuminara**  
Ker ponavljamo tisto, kar ljubimo. Vsaka ponovitev postane še ena pot domov. Več poti ko ima spomin, koristnejši je za sporočilo, ki poskuša preživeti to razdaljo.

**Bartosz**  
Potem je tat, ki ne ve, da krade.

**Illuminara**  
Ali poštar, ki vsak paket obloži s pohištvom, ki ga je mogoče znova sestaviti. Zaradi tega mu ne bi odpustila. Bi pa vedela, kakšno pohištvo naj postavim ob vrata.

Soren je v šestih minutah obnovil kalibracijsko matriko iz trezorja. Nihče v oddelku ni rekel, da jezika iz trezorja ne more obnoviti nič. Bartosz je kartico zgibal vse manjšo in manjšo, dokler je ni bilo mogoče več prepogniti.

scenes.title: Pohištvo
paragraphs: *Tretje tovorno skladišče · 14:30*

Prva mreža je bila Illuminarin načrt, zgradila pa jo je posadka. Kristal hladilne tekočine se je iz krova dvignil v prozornem ogrodju. Vanj so snemali dnevni dnevnik, števce motorjev in kuhinjske pesmi, dokler skladišče ni vsebovalo devetsto kopij vsakega.
Vztrajala je pri treh pravilih in jih izrekla na glas, da bi jim lahko ugovarjali.

**Illuminara**  
Nihče ne vnese ničesar, za čimer bi žaloval. Samo kopije, nikoli izvirnikov, in ničesar, kar bi bilo edina kopija česarkoli. Mreža je namenoma poceni. Vsak lahko zavrne. Kdor zavrne, ga ne vprašamo več.

**Soren**  
Fotografije moje žene ne bodo šle v ta kristal.

**Illuminara**  
Ne bodo. Pa tudi vi ne.
Dolgo jo je gledal. Nato je odšel v kuhinjo in začel snemalniku devetstokrat razglašeno peti večerno pesem.

Bartosza je prosila za kartico. Pod svoji dve napovedi je z isto pisavo zapisala tretjo: *Devetsto kopij bo služilo kot gostitelj.* Prepognjeno mu je vrnila, nato pa ga prosila, naj iz mreže izbriše eno pesem.

Ostalo je osemsto devetindevetdeset enakih kopij, vendar nobena ni vsebovala razmerja, ki bi lahko povedalo, kaj je bilo izbrisano, namesto da bi to zgolj nadomestilo z drugim klonom. Prikaz rekonstrukcije je ostal rdeč.

**Bartosz**  
Kup enakih stolov. Med njimi ni prostora.

**Illuminara**  
Prikaz se ne strinja z mojo tretjo vrstico. Napoved, ki se ne strinja s svojim instrumentom, je vseeno vredna pošiljanja, zato bomo ugotovili, kdo od njiju se moti.

Mrežo klonov so poslali z nepomembnim vprašanjem. Šum se ni zložil. Štiri ure je šumenje med galaksijami ostalo šumenje in v teh štirih urah je Moreau z glasom, ki ga je ohranjala zelo mirnega, rekla, da jih je Knjižnica morda zavrnila.
Illuminara tišine ni preimenovala v uspeh. Bartosza je prosila, naj odpre kartico, in sama pod tretjo vrstico zapisala NI USPELO.

**Illuminara**  
Sklop je preživel izbris, ker so se njegove razlike medsebojno preverjale. Stena enakih stolov tega ne zmore. Prikaz je imel prav, jaz pa sem se motila.

Nato je v gostitelja vgradila raznolikost. Vsaka pesem je bila odpeta v drugem ključu, z drugačno hitrostjo in drugačno mešanico glasov. Števci motorjev so bili razvrščeni prek neodvisnih ur. Dnevniki so bili razdeljeni na odlomke, katerih paritetne črte so križale pesmi, ne da bi jih vsebovale. Wren Odira, ki je prišla na krov s kurirsko ladjo in pela razglašeno, je prispevala štirideset posnetkov, ki jih ni mogel ponoviti nihče drug.
Izbrisali so vsak osmi odlomek. Mreža je vsakega obnovila iz razmerij, ki so križala različno gradivo. Prikaz se je obarval zeleno: enakih devet devetk kot pri raziskovalni matriki.

**Wren**  
Dovolj grdo?

**Illuminara**  
Dovolj bogato. Lahko izgubi del sebe in še vedno ve, kaj je sodilo tja.
Na začetek kode so postavili izjavo: GOSTITELJSKA MREŽA TRI. Nič v izjavi ni imenovalo človeka. Nič ni kazalo na ladijsko zdravstveno omrežje.

Preden so karkoli poslali, je vsakega človeka na krovu prosila, naj na listek zapečati eno stvar, ki jo je tisti dan še lahko imenoval in za katero bi žaloval, če bi jo izgubil. Moreau je zapisala ime svoje hčere. Soren je zapisal ulico, kjer je zaprosil ženo. Bartosz, ki ni imel več ničesar iz Lowvala, kar bi varoval, je zapisal datum babičine smrti, edino dejstvo o njej, ki je še držalo.
Soren je sklop nastavil tako, da je poslal vprašanje. Nihče ni stal pri pultu in nihče se ga ni dotaknil. Vprašal je po številu motornih ciklov od zadnje prenove.

Šum se je zložil. Odgovor je prispel in ladijski dnevniki so ga potrdili do cikla natančno. V skladišču so se paritetna razmerja mreže spremenila v šum, posnetki pa so v trezorju ostali celi. Nato so drug za drugim odprli listke in vsakega primerjali z umom, ki ga je napisal. Vse na listkih je ostalo.

**Hadiza**  
Vzelo je gostitelja. Samo gostitelja.

**Illuminara**  
Enkrat. Pred nami, ko ni bilo nikogar pri pultu. To je en preizkus, en preizkus pa še ni pravilo. Toda prvič smo videli nekaj, kar nam pove, da izjava spremeni, kam piše.

Moreau je prvo pravo vprašanje zastavila sama. Zdaj tega ni zahtevalo nič. Storila je zato, ker ne bi nikogar poslala stati tja, kjer sama ne bi stala, in ker bi morala kapitanka, ki zaupa rezultatu, nanj lahko položiti roko. Vprašala je stoje, z dlanjo plosko na pultu, segla po svojem imenu in njeno ime je bilo tam.
Kristal je rahlo zazvenel, kakor kozarec, ki se ga je nekdo dotaknil.

scenes.title: Pravilo
paragraphs: *Ladijska dolga soba · 212. ladijski dan, 02:15*

Odgovor ni bil številka. Bil je oblika in potrebovali so štiri ure, da so ga prebrali. Pred pošiljanjem česarkoli zadržite nespremenljiv delež zaloge vsakega sveta. Sproščajte ne sorazmerno s pomanjkanjem, temveč sorazmerno z zamikom med naročilom in prihodom. Kaskada, je rekla Illuminara, je bila zvenenje: vsaka ladja je popravljala lakoto, ki je bila že teden dni stara, popravki pa so stradali naslednji svet v vrsti.
Odgovor je bil natančen in imel je dve praznini. Delež in zamik. Knjižnica ni nikoli videla knjigovodskih knjig flote, zato ju ni mogla zapolniti.

Prosila je za dnevnike vseh ladij in knjige vseh treh svetov, jih postavila drugo ob drugo in iskala tisto, kar se ni ujemalo. Minila je tretja ura, preden je našla. Žitni konvoj iz Tarna, osemnajst ladij, je dosegel Veyrina vrata devet dni po odhodu. Tarnova knjiga ga je štirinajst dni vodila kot tovor na poti. Veyrina knjiga ga ni štela, dokler carina štirinajsti dan ni ožigosala manifesta.

**Illuminara**  
Pet dni je to žito stalo v skladišču pri Veyrinih vratih in ni bilo v nobeni knjigi. Tarn ga je odpisal. Veyra ga še ni vpisala. Vsi svetovi naprej v vrsti berejo žige, ne žita.

**Soren**  
En konvoj. Naključje.

**Illuminara**  
Preverila sem štirideset najbližjih. V vsakem se pojavi ista vrzel, med tremi in štirimi odstotki odhodne zaloge v kateremkoli tridnevnem oknu. Pomanjkanje, ki obstaja samo na papirju.

**Hadiza**  
Potem je del lakote žig.

**Illuminara**  
Del zvenenja je. To zapolni praznini. Pravi zamik je devet dni, ne štirinajst. In vse pod štirimi odstotki pojasnijo žigi. Če odhodna zaloga v dveh zaporednih tridnevnih oknih preseže vhodno za več kot štiri odstotke, je lakota resnična. Zadržanje se takoj spremeni. Noben svet ne čaka, da čudovit model prizna svojo zmoto.
Nihče na ladji Reach ni vzkliknil. Gledali so vrstico, ki je določala, da mora Ossel enajst dni zadrževati svoje zaloge, medtem ko bo njegovim ljudem primanjkovalo hrane.
Osselov delegat Aurelio Quist se je na povezavi z zamikom prikazal v sivi svetlobi svojega jutra, štirideset minut za besedami, na katere je odgovarjal.

**Aurelio Quist**  
Od mojih ljudi zahtevate, naj enajst dni sedijo ob polnih skladiščih na besedo glasu v šumu. Moji južni okraji so lačni zdaj. Tega ne bom podpisal.

**Illuminara**  
Ne morem podpisati namesto vas in ne bom poskušala. Vam smem pokazati celoten dušeni model z njegovim robom napake, konvoj, ki nam je dal zamik, in kraje, kjer najprej prizadene Ossel?
Pokazala mu je. Pokazala mu je dve knjigi konvoja Marrow drugo ob drugi in južne okraje v rdečem. Ni jih skrila za povprečjem.

**Aurelio Quist**  
Osem dni, ne enajst. Bolnišnice in šolske kuhinje so po pravici izvzete iz zadržanja. In moji analitiki dobijo surovo knjigo, ne vaših zaključkov.

**Illuminara**  
Vaš lastni seznam bolnišnicam in šolskim kuhinjam pripisuje enajst odstotkov Osselove porabe. Dodajte tri točke, da se lahko izjema izmenjuje z javnim žrebom in je noben okraj ne more kupiti, pa osem dni deluje. Štirinajst odstotkov. Vaši analitiki naj imajo pogoj za ustavitev skupaj z našimi. Knjižnico lahko prosim, naj preveri račun. Plačal bo gostitelj, ne um.

**Hadiza**  
Še ena mreža.

**Wren**  
Imam še šeststo pesmi. Vse so razglašene.

Drugi odgovor je prispel ob zori in potrdil račun: osem dni s štirinajstodstotno izmenjujočo se izjemo je napoved ohranilo znotraj meja, ki so jih Quistovi analitiki lahko ponovili iz surove knjige. Ni obljubil, da bo kogarkoli rešil vseh posledic. Njegovim južnim okrajem bo tri tedne primanjkovalo hrane in nekateri stari ter zelo mladi morda ne bodo preživeli. Quist je podpisal z opozorilom ob svojem imenu, ker brez njega ni hotel podpisati.

scenes.title: Česar ni bilo vrnjenega
paragraphs: *Opazovalna paluba · 274. ladijski dan, 21:00*
Odkar je prvo pravilo vstopilo v floto, je minilo enainšestdeset dni. Tisto jutro so analitiki Tarna, Veyre in sveta Ossel podpisali ločene knjige, ne da bi si prej razkrili sklepe.

Tarnove zaloge niso nikoli dosegle praznine in zdaj so obsegale devetnajst dni hrane. Veyra je dosegla dno pri dvanajstih odstotkih rezerve, nato pa je enaindvajset zaporednih dni naraščala. Osselovi južni okraji so prestali napovedano pomanjkanje; umrlo je sto triinosemdeset ljudi, katerih smrt so delegati ocenili kot povezano z lakoto. Štirideset milijonov je bila številka, ki so jo dale stare odredbe, ko so dnevnike flote pognali naprej brez pravila. Bila je napoved in vsaka knjiga je to jasno povedala. Knjige so zapisovale le, kar se je zgodilo.

Štiriodstotni sprožilec se je sprožil enkrat, na Veyri. Osselovi analitiki so zahtevali dogovorjeni popravek, trije konvoji so obrnili in naslednji dve okni sta se vrnili pod prag. Pravilu niso zaupali. Opazovali so ga.

Preden se je pomožna flota razpršila, je posadka izvedla še en preizkus, ki ga lakota ni zahtevala, nadzorovano različico tega, kar so nekoč že videli. Zgradili so dva neškodljiva samoobnovljiva gostitelja, jantarnega in modrega, oba z istim nepomembnim vprašanjem in različnim naključnim enkratnim nizom. Izjava je imenovala jantarnega.
Knjižnica je odgovorila enkrat. Jantarjeva paritetna razmerja so izginila. Modri je ostal cel.
Očistili so krajevni sprejemnik, oba gostitelja obnovili iz nedotaknjenih varnostnih kopij, zamenjali njuni mesti in imenovali modrega. Knjižnica je znova odgovorila. Modri je plačal. Jantarni ni.

Nato je Knjižnica storila nekaj, česar ni še nikoli. Sto štiri sekunde je šum pri pultu prevzel preprosto ponavljajočo se obliko: prazno polje gostitelja, za njim pa enkratni niz, ki so ji ga ponudili. Ni rekla da. Vprašala je kam.

**Hadiza**  
Dvakrat še ni vest.

**Illuminara**  
Ne. Je pa izbira, ki jo lahko ločimo od izpada, krajevnega oblikovanja ali naključja. Vemo, da lahko sledi razglašenemu gostitelju. Ne vemo, kaj zanjo pomeni slediti.

**Bartosz**  
Torej je bil to jezik, ki se ga nismo naučili.

**Illuminara**  
Prva beseda enega. Še vedno lahko zavrne gostitelja. Še vedno lahko molči. Le človeka smo nehali postavljati za privzeti naslov.
Bartosz je stal pri steklu s hrbtom proti njim. Čez čas je spregovoril previdno, kakor človek, ki govori v drugem jeziku.

**Bartosz**  
Ali ga lahko mreža vrne? Lowvale. Sebe bi dal v kristal, če bi ga to vrnilo.
Illuminara bi veliko dala, da bi lahko odgovorila drugače.

**Illuminara**  
Ne. Knjižnica je vzela edino kopijo, ki je kadarkoli živela v vas, v mreži pa ni ničesar, kar bi bilo njena kopija. Lahko vam zgradim boljše ogrodje. Ne morem vam zgraditi babice. Če bi rekla, da lahko, bi vam počela to, kar je storila Knjižnica, le z nežnejšim glasom.
Pokimal je in se ni obrnil. Nato je Wren, ki je pela razglašeno, prosil, naj ga nauči eno svojih pesmi. Rekel je, da ima veliko prostora.

Calderjevi svetovi so dovolili eno vprašanje na štirinajst dni, nič več. Vsako vprašanje je zahtevalo imenovanega zunanjega gostitelja, dva uspešna preizkusa rekonstrukcije, javno soglasje za uporabljeno gradivo in neodvisnega opazovalca, ki je držal ključ za ustavitev. Nobenega človeka niso prosili, naj pozabi, kako kanal narediti varen.
Illuminara sama Knjižnice ni vprašala ničesar. Nekaj časa je ostala pri pultu in šum je pod njeno dlanjo ležal tih.
*Popoln odgovor,* je pomislila, *je bil ves čas samo slabo naslovljen.*

translation_sl.critic_line: Tihi knjižnici, ki za vsak odgovor zaračuna spomin, ne odgovori sila, temveč preizkus, ki bi se lahko motil; Illuminarina potrpežljivost, njena lastna spodletela napoved in nepravilnost v knjigi tovornega prometa nahranijo tri svetove, ne da bi za to plačal še en človek.
